family.name: UX / Product Designer
family.summary: A checkout losing a third of users at one step: find the problem from funnel data and usability notes, pick the fix that fits two weeks, and catch the accessibility problems in a proposed screen.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where is checkout breaking?
stages.summary: Use funnel data, usability notes and a heatmap to find the real problem: the address step, for specific reasons. Think aloud.

stages.title: What fits in two weeks
stages.summary: Choose a fix for one engineer for two weeks. Tests scoping to the evidence. Think aloud.

stages.title: After launch
stages.summary: Results of their choice arrive. Tests reading results and adapting.

stages.title: Review a proposed screen
stages.summary: A new address screen spec with placeholder-only labels, colour-only errors, small tap targets and low contrast. Think aloud.

stages.title: Error messages (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the address-form error messages with AI. Catches vague, blaming copy.

stages.title: A design you changed after testing
stages.summary: A real design they changed after seeing users struggle. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're a product designer at **Tiffinly**, a home-cooked meal subscription app. 87% of users are on phones, 56% of them on low-cost Android phones. 97% of people who reach checkout are already logged in.
Usability test notes (6 participants, on their own phones)

items: 5 of 6 typed their PIN code with a space ("560 034") and saw "Invalid PIN" with no explanation. The PIN field opens the letter keyboard.
3 of 6 stopped at the required "Landmark" field: "My building doesn't have one."
Two people moved the map pin by accident while scrolling, and their address changed.
One person said the colours "look a bit dull" on the payment page.

brief.text: The heatmap shows people tapping the greyed-out "Continue" button on the address step an average of 27 times per 100 visits. Nothing explains why it is disabled.
Engineering can give you **one engineer for 2 weeks** this cycle.
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Describe a small design detail in an app you use that you think is great.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Where is checkout losing people, and why?** Rank the causes you see, most damaging first, and say how sure you are of each.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Add a progress bar and trust badges

prompt.text: **What do you ask the engineer to build in 2 weeks?** Pick one, list exactly what changes, and say how you'll know it worked.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Redesign the whole checkout"

prompt.text: After two weeks only the cart and address screens are redesigned; the rest will take 4 more weeks. The half-new, half-old flow looks inconsistent, and the PM asks whether to ship it as is.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Fix the address step only"

prompt.text: The address step now continues at 80%. But support says some users in apartment blocks now get deliveries at the wrong gate, since "Landmark" became optional.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: Guest checkout shipped. The address step still loses about the same share of users, and the PM asks why nothing moved.
**What do you say and do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Add a progress bar and trust badges"

prompt.text: Address-step continuation moved by 0.8 points, within normal week-to-week noise. The marketing team loves the new badges and wants them on every page.
**What do you do?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A teammate proposes this new address screen. **Name the most serious problems, worst first, and who each one hurts.** Then describe your fixes.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: Single column of fields, one per row.
Field names shown only as placeholder text inside the boxes (e.g. "Flat / House no."); they disappear when you start typing.
Placeholder text in light grey #BDBDBD on white.
If a field is wrong, its border turns red. No message.
"Save address" and "Cancel" are the same size and colour, side by side at the bottom.
The "use current location" link is 12 px text, about 28 × 18 px to tap.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.

Write the error and help messages for the address form (each under 60 characters): PIN code wrong, PIN code outside the delivery area, house number missing, the disabled "Continue" button, and the location permission being denied.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: A design you changed after testing

prompt.text: **Tell us about a design of yours that changed after you watched people use it.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
